title: Implicit logspace closure under guarded composition
statement: Let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words and suppose its output length is bounded by a polynomial in the input length, while the languages of encoded pairs $\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle$ for which the $i$-th bit of $f(x)$ is true and for which $i<|f(x)|$ are decidable in logarithmic space. Define a function on Boolean words $w$ by parsing $w$ as $\langle x,b\rangle$; if parsing succeeds and $b$ is the binary representation of its own value, return $\langle f(x),b\rangle$, and otherwise return the empty word. This function has polynomially bounded output length, and its true-bit index language and output-length index language are both decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: The true-bit index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
The output-length index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
